settings.title: LSP diagnostics
settings.global.autoInject.label: Auto-inject (global)
settings.global.autoInject.hint: On: a project joining DSH for the first time is configured automatically, and compile errors are echoed to the AI after edits.
Off: new projects are only registered, never configured automatically.
settings.global.autoAddon.label: Auto-install the Godot engine bridge
settings.global.autoAddon.hint: On: a project missing the Godot engine bridge gets it installed automatically. The bridge is a Godot editor plugin placed inside the project, which adds an addons/dsh_echo_bridge directory and enables it in project.godot.

The bridge only means anything to Godot, and it does two things. It lets a running engine accept a rescan request, so a class_name in a new script is no longer reported as an unknown type. And it lets the post-edit refresh first confirm whether a script has unsaved changes, so it cannot overwrite what you are editing.
Off: the plugin never changes your project on its own. Use the "Install Godot engine bridge" button on the project card instead; installing again updates it in place.
settings.about.title: How it works
settings.about.body: A project is a directory, and it can contain several languages, GDScript and C# for example. Each language gets its own engine, which claims its file extensions and reports diagnostics to the AI when those files are compiled or edited.
"Smart config" scans a project and adds the engines that are missing. It only adds; it never overrides a configuration you removed by hand.
settings.about.config: "Smart config" scans a project and adds only the LSPs that are missing. It never overrides one you removed by hand.
A project you edited shows as "Manual" and can be reset to its configured seed at any time.
settings.projects.title: Projects
settings.projects.register.title: Pick a DSH workspace project to register. Projects without GDScript are accepted: registering one only reserves a slot and produces no diagnostics.
settings.projects.none: No DSH workspace project is available to register
settings.projects.add.title: Register the selected DSH project with the chosen engine
settings.projects.smartAll.title: Detect each unconfigured project's languages and add the missing LSPs
settings.engines.title: Engines (LSP)
settings.engines.body: An engine is the checker for one language. A project can contain several languages, and each one gets its own engine.
Each engine claims its own file extensions: the Godot engine claims .gd and .gdshader. When those files are compiled or edited, the engine reports diagnostics back to the AI.
The "editor LSP port" is the language-server port the Godot editor opens for itself. The plugin connects to it to read the live diagnostics from your editor. The default is 6005.
If you changed that port in Godot under Editor Settings > Network > Language Server > Remote Port, enter it here and save, and the plugin stops guessing.

Ports are set per project. Two Godot projects share one engine, but each opens its own editor on its own port. If you only fill in the "All projects" row, the second project's editor looks like it is serving a different project, so the connection is refused and the plugin falls back to headless mode.
Clearing a row's input and saving removes that row's setting, so the "All projects" value applies again.

toast.enginePort.title: {name} editor LSP port problem
toast.enginePort.wrongProject: The language server on port {ports} serves a different project, not the one being checked, so it cannot diagnose this project. Its empty replies would pass off as "0 errors".
The plugin switched to its own engine. Once you switch the editor back to this project, that port is retried after its 5-minute blacklist expires.
toast.enginePort.ownConflict: Port {ports} was taken by this plugin's own headless engine: starting it also opens Godot's debug adapter (DAP) default port, which collided with the editor LSP port you reserved in the settings. Your editor is not at fault.
The plugin stopped that engine and now starts it with arguments that avoid reserved ports, so the port is free again for your editor.
toast.enginePort.engineHoldsPort: Port {ports} became busy after this plugin started its engine, and the engine is the likely holder: this Godot build may not know --dap-port, so it opened the DAP default (6006).
The engine keeps running, so diagnostics still work. To free that port for your editor, set the editor LSP port to something other than 6006 (6008, say), or use Godot 4.3+ which honours --dap-port.
toast.enginePort.noReply: Port {ports} accepts connections but does not answer LSP requests: the process holding it is not that language's editor LSP, or the editor LSP is stuck.
The plugin switched to its own engine; check that port.
